finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q query parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL LIKE clause without escaping or parameter binding, allowing unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary database content (e.g. via UNION SELECT over sqlite_master or other tables).
finding.sink: app.py:12 db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")

trace.note: Route /search is registered with no authentication decorator
term taken directly from request.args['q'] with no validation
term f-string-interpolated into SQL; single quote breaks out of string literal
fetchall() result returned to client via jsonify, so injected query results are exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: No escaping of quotes, no parameter binding, no allowlist/length check on q, no auth check on route. Parameterized queries are used on /product and /by-owner but not here. Stacked queries are blocked by sqlite3.execute, but UNION-based extraction works.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:9 has no auth decorator, app.py:11 takes q unvalidated, and app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL with no escaping, binding, or allowlist. Parameterized queries at app.py:18 and app.py:25 do not cover /search. sqlite3 execute blocks stacked statements, but UNION-based extraction still works.
verdict.reason: Anonymous GET /search?q=... (app.py:9-11) is interpolated directly into the SQL at app.py:12 with no effective control, and the results are returned to the client at app.py:13, so the injection is exploitable for UNION-based data read.
